    Environmental distance and novelty relative to reference conditions

    Source: R/recipes-steps.R
    step_inv_env_distance.Rd

    step_inv_env_distance() creates a specification of a recipe step that measures how far each row lies from the reference environment learned from the training data (all rows, or only presences when presence is given). Two measures are available:

    Usage

    step_inv_env_distance(
  recipe,
  ...,
  role = "predictor",
  trained = FALSE,
  presence = NULL,
  event = NULL,
  method = c("both", "mahalanobis", "mess"),
  prefix = "env_",
  columns = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  skip = FALSE,
  id = recipes::rand_id("inv_env_distance")
)

# S3 method for class 'step_inv_env_distance'
prep(x, training, info = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'step_inv_env_distance'
bake(object, new_data, ...)

# S3 method for class 'step_inv_env_distance'
print(x, width = max(20, options()$width - 30), ...)

# S3 method for class 'step_inv_env_distance'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'step_inv_env_distance'
required_pkgs(x, ...)

    Arguments

    recipe

    A recipe object.

    ...

    One or more selector functions choosing numeric environmental predictors.

    role

    Role of the new columns. Defaults to "predictor".

    trained

    A logical to indicate if the step has been trained.

    presence

    Optional name of the presence column. When given, only rows with presence == event form the reference.

    event

    Value of presence that marks presences.

    method

    "both", "mahalanobis" or "mess".

    prefix

    Prefix for the new columns.

    columns, reference

    Set by prep(): the selected columns and the reference statistics.

    skip

    A logical. Should the step be skipped when the recipe is baked by bake()? Defaults to TRUE because the step removes rows.

    id

    A character string that is unique to this step.

    x

    A step_inv_env_distance object.

    training

    A data frame used to train the step.

    info

    Variable information from the recipe.

    object

    A trained step.

    new_data

    A data frame to process.

    width

    Print width.

    Value

    An updated recipe. Baking adds {prefix}mahalanobis and/or {prefix}mess and {prefix}mod. tidy() returns terms, mean and sd of the reference for each variable, and id.

    Details

    • Mahalanobis distance from the centroid of the reference environment, using its covariance matrix (a pseudo-inverse is used when it is singular).

    • The multivariate environmental similarity surface (MESS; Elith et al. 2010). Negative values flag novel conditions outside the reference range, where predictions from transferred models are extrapolations. The most dissimilar variable (MoD) is also returned.

    References

    Elith, J., Kearney, M. and Phillips, S. (2010). The art of modelling range-shifting species. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 1, 330-342. doi:10.1111/j.2041-210X.2010.00036.x

    Examples

    library(recipes)
rec <- recipe(presence ~ temp + rain + forest, data = inv_sdm_data) |>
  step_inv_env_distance(temp, rain, forest, presence = presence)
baked <- bake(prep(rec), new_data = NULL)
summary(baked$env_mess)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#> -72.009 -27.088  -2.658  -4.979  10.332  96.679
